purpose: Repaglinide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works best when taken with meals to prevent blood sugar from spiking after you eat. It is usually used along with healthy eating and exercise.
how_it_works: Your pancreas has special cells that make insulin, the hormone that lowers your blood sugar. Repaglinide tells those cells to release more insulin, but only when you eat, so it helps handle the sugar that comes from your meal. Because it only works when you are eating, it acts fast and wears off quickly.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can make you feel shaky, sweaty, dizzy, or confused. You may also notice headache, upper respiratory infections, back pain, or mild stomach upset. Weight gain can sometimes occur with long-term use.
warnings: Always take this medicine right before a meal — if you skip a meal, skip that dose too, to avoid dangerously low blood sugar. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as the medicine can build up in your body. Drinking alcohol can increase your risk of low blood sugar. Some medicines, including certain antifungals and antibiotics, can interact with repaglinide and change how it works, so always check with your pharmacist before starting anything new.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 0.5 mg taken 15 to 30 minutes before each main meal (up to 3 times a day). Your doctor may increase your dose over time up to a maximum of 4 mg per meal (16 mg per day). If you skip a meal, skip that dose. Never double up doses.
